Header: Ralstonia solanacearum Bangla name: Dholepora Rog of Tomato

Prevention: Try to select fields with no history of bacterial wilt.
Remove volunteer host plants and solanaceous weeds like
Crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops, e.g. peas, cowpea, cauliflower, rice, maize, beans etc.
Grow seedlings in solarised soil, virgin soil or peat moss.
Grow crops in ridge and furrow system.
Avoid root injury during intercultural operations.
Use seedlings grafted onto wilt resistant wild eggplant (Solanum sisymbriifolium).
Apply stable bleaching powder @ 20-25kg/ha 7 days before transplanting seedlings.
Monitoring: Monitor crop daily for sudden wilting of plants in the field.
Check for vascular discoloration in basal stem of wilted plants.
Split the stem at the bottom of the plant and look for brown staining inside.
Perform streaming test by putting the lower part of a cut stem in still water in a clear bottle and carefully looking for milky strands of bacterial ooze streaming from the cut surface.
Take action as soon as you have observed a single wilted plant.
Direct Control: Uproot and bury infected plants (at least 30 cm deep) outside the field or burn immediately after identification.
Drain field as quickly as possible after rains.
Isolate the diseased area by making furrows to reduce the spread of bacteria to non-infested parts of the field.
